briefing:
The Reserve Bank of India and MoSPI daily airfare intelligence pipeline generated a headline daily Airfare Price Index (APIx) reading of 0.0, representing a nominal -100.0% shift relative to base period benchmarks. Econometric analysis indicates that this macro aggregate readout is an operational artifact resulting from data ingestion warnings, wherein secondary and regional routes were excluded due to string-matching discrepancies between baseline records and target scrape key formats. Consequently, active aggregate index weight temporarily fell to zero for the broader basket. However, direct evaluation of fully matched primary trunk routes reveals a market environment defined by robust yield strength. On the high-density Delhi–Mumbai corridor—which carries a substantial 3.33% weight in the macro weighting scheme—target day medians exceeded baseline figures across all advance booking horizons, confirming firm underlying market demand along major domestic travel arteries.

A granular comparison of base medians against target day scraped medians on the Delhi–Mumbai route highlights significant upward pressure across the entire forward booking curve. In the immediate departure window ($T+1$, September 21, 2026), the target median price surged to ₹14,293 against a base median of ₹6,530, reflecting a 118.9% increase driven by tight short-haul capacity and business travel demand. The $T+7$ window (September 27, 2026) similarly escalated to a median of ₹12,572 compared to its ₹6,373 baseline (+97.3%). Further along the booking timeline, $T+15$ medians rose from ₹6,530 to ₹9,174 (+40.5%), $T+30$ medians increased from ₹6,530 to ₹9,527 (+45.9%), and $T+45$ medians advanced from ₹6,684 to ₹11,380.5 (+70.3%). This systematic uplift across medium- and long-dated windows demonstrates that pricing momentum extends well beyond last-minute travel demand, establishing an elevated forward fare floor for October and early November 2026 travel dates.

Examination of the granular scrape dataset reveals broad intra-day price dispersion and notable carrier pricing dynamics on the Delhi–Mumbai corridor. For $T+1$ departures, single-seat economy prices ranged from a low of ₹5,969 on SpiceJet (SG-2802) to a high of ₹33,500 on IndiGo (6E-675) for late-available or flexible inventory, alongside multi-segment Air India Express itineraries pricing up to ₹24,123. On $T+7$, Akasa Air offered the lowest entry fare at ₹4,847 (QP-1940), contrasting sharply with Air India Express connecting routes that reached ₹28,319. Across all sampled dates, the observed fare inflation was heavily concentrated in the base fare component, while statutory taxes and airport charges remained bounded within a narrow range of ₹1,400 to ₹2,600 for direct routes.

Looking forward, the elevated fare profile across advance windows points to persistent cost pressures in the civil aviation sector, which could exert upward pass-through effects on the transport and communication sub-index of the Consumer Price Index (CPI). From a policy perspective, while the immediate focus for technical teams must be resolving string-matching dictionaries within the automated pipeline to restore aggregate APIx calculation, the empirical price trends on key commercial corridors indicate firm service-sector demand. RBI and MoSPI monitoring units should maintain close surveillance on major trunk route yields as an early indicator of core services inflation, while ensuring pipeline remediation to provide uninterrupted macro index tracking through the upcoming peak travel season.
